findings.checklist_item: Name the durable artifact (e.g. a per-run tidy epic grouping its child tickets) by which the next run enumerates exactly the previous run's tickets, and reconcile it with the 'no counter/tag/state of its own' rule so the two are not contradictory.
evidence: Plan: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets and summing the merged diffs of exactly those'
Plan: 'the skill adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own, because a skill that exists to remove mechanism must not install any'
ticketization.md:10 — existing run grouping is the dated epic 'Janitor Cleanup <YYYY-MM-DD>' with one child per remediation
ABSENCE: the plan never names the durable artifact (e.g. a per-run epic) that lets a later run enumerate 'exactly' a prior run's tickets without new state
findings.finding: The attribution mechanism requires the next run to read 'exactly' the previous run's tickets, but the plan simultaneously forbids the skill from adding 'any counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own', leaving no stated artifact by which run N+1 enumerates run N's tickets. The existing janitor groups a run's children under a dated 'Janitor Cleanup <YYYY-MM-DD>' epic (ticketization.md:10), which would resolve this, but the plan does not say the tidy skill keeps a per-run grouping epic.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets' and 'the skill adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own'
scenarios: Run N+1 begins and must list run N's tickets, but there is no named grouping (no epic, no tag) and inventing one would violate the no-state rule
Two tidy runs occur close together and their tickets cannot be disambiguated into 'the previous run's' set
findings.suggested_fix: State that the tidy skill files its run's tickets under a single dated per-run epic (reusing the existing 'Janitor Cleanup <YYYY-MM-DD>'-style grouping), and clarify that an epic grouping is the tracker's native parent/child relation — not new skill-owned state — so the next run reads that epic's children to obtain 'exactly those' tickets.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the next run identifies the previous run's ticket set (e.g. a dated epic the run files its tickets under, reusing the existing 'Janitor Cleanup <date>' epic as the identity anchor rather than new skill state) and reconcile that with the 'no counter/tag/persistent state of its own' constraint so the attribution step is deterministic.
evidence: Plan: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets and summing the merged diffs of exactly those'
Plan: 'the skill adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own, because a skill that exists to remove mechanism must not install any'

The existing run-identity anchor is the dated epic title 'Janitor Cleanup <YYYY-MM-DD>' (examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/ticketization.md:10) and the '.rebar-janitor/report-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md' file (SKILL.md:100) — both arguably forbidden as the tidying skill's own state
ABSENCE: the plan names the measuring actor and when (next run's opening step) but never the rule that maps a run to its ticket set under the no-state constraint
findings.finding: The tidying janitor's next-run attribution protocol references 'the previous run's tickets' and 'exactly those' but defines no mechanism for identifying that ticket set, while the plan simultaneously forbids the skill any counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own.
findings.location: Plan section 'The change — modify, not discard', bullets 'a run is scored by what LANDED, attributed to the run' and 'the skill adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own'; AC lines 'Its success metric is what merged from the run's own tickets' and 'It introduces no counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own.'
scenarios: Second tidying run opens, must read 'the previous run's tickets,' but two prior runs' tickets coexist in the tracker with no run tag or state to distinguish them
A prior-run ticket was refined/retitled by the operator, so a title-prefix heuristic silently drops it from the attributed set — defeating the 'ones never merged' visibility the AC requires
findings.suggested_fix: State that the prior run is identified by its dated cleanup epic (the tracker artifact the operator already approves), not by any new tag or counter — the epic's child set IS the run's ticket set — so attribution reuses existing tracker structure and the no-new-state rule still holds.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name (or specify creation of) the test that proves neither skill names a specific model/vendor, e.g. a new test that greps both SKILL trees for a vendor/model denylist and asserts zero matches.
evidence: AC: 'Neither skill names a specific model or vendor. Verified by a test.'
Plan grounding names only frontmatter, concern_schema, and shared_sync checks — none assert model/vendor absence
The 'Provider neutrality' section states both skills 'must not assume a vendor's model, tool-calling syntax, or harness' but no proving command is tied to it
findings.finding: The acceptance criterion 'Neither skill names a specific model or vendor. Verified by a test.' asserts a test proves it, but the plan never names that test nor specifies creating one. The three tests named in Plan grounding (check_skill_frontmatter.py, test_janitor_concern_schema.py, test_skill_shared_sync.py) do not assert vendor/model neutrality.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — final bullet ('Verified by a test'); Plan grounding command list
scenarios: Executor finishes both skills, cannot find or build the neutrality test, and must stop to ask which test satisfies this AC
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Plan-grounding bullet: `tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py` (new) scans every file under both skill directories for a denylist of vendor/model tokens and asserts none appear; the AC's proving command is `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py`.

findings.checklist_item: Address the terminal/most-recent run: state how its landed deletions are scored when no successor run exists (e.g. an operator-invoked score-only pass over a prior run's epic).
evidence: Plan: scoring is defined only as an action of 'the NEXT run'
ABSENCE: no provision for scoring a run that has no successor (program wind-down, or simply the most recent run at any point in time)
findings.finding: The next-run-scores-previous-run design has an unhandled terminal case: the final tidy run's deletions are never scored because no subsequent run opens to measure them. The plan presents attribution as if a successor run always exists.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets'
scenarios: The operator wants to know whether the most recent tidy run actually removed what it declared, but no later run has been triggered
Tidying is discontinued; the last run's effectiveness is never reported

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the first run (no prior) and the final/latest run (no successor) are scored — e.g. the operator may invoke the opening measurement step standalone against the last run's tickets without starting a new run.
evidence: 'a run is scored by what LANDED, attributed to the run: the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets'
AC: 'It names the measuring actor and when: the next run's opening step.'
ABSENCE: no described step scores a run when there is no following run (final run), nor bootstraps the first run
findings.finding: The run-scoring mechanism is defined only as 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets'. This leaves the first run with no prior run to score and — more consequentially — the most-recent run is never scored because no subsequent run exists to read it. The plan does not describe how the final/latest run's effectiveness is ever measured.
findings.location: 'The change' section — scoring/attribution bullets; AC 'It names the measuring actor and when: the next run's opening step.'
scenarios: Operator wants to know whether the latest tidying run actually removed mechanism, but the metric is only ever produced by a run that never comes
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bullet: the measuring step is runnable independently of starting a new discovery pass, so the operator can score the most recent run on demand; the first run reports 'no prior run to attribute'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly, for each of the three 'never edits code' statements, which skill(s) retain them after the split — in particular whether the tidying janitor keeps 'never edits code' given it only files deletion tickets.
evidence: Plan grounding: '"Never edits code" is stated three times and all three move with the split: SKILL.md:14 ... :68 ... :127'
The change: tidying janitor 'whose only admissible outputs are deletions and collapses' and 'each ticket it files declares the deletion it will make'
The gap point 2 criticises '"Never edits code" turns tidying into ticket generation' — so its disposition in the new skills is load-bearing and under-specified
findings.finding: The plan says the three 'Never edits code' statements (SKILL.md:14, :68, :127) 'all move with the split' but never states which skill retains them. The tidying janitor's admissible outputs are 'deletions and collapses' and it 'files' tickets — so whether 'never edits code' applies to the tidying janitor, the defect audit, or both is left to the executor.
findings.location: Plan grounding — "Never edits code" paragraph; 'The change' section
scenarios: Executor must decide whether the tidying janitor's SKILL.md frontmatter (read by the harness to decide invocation) keeps the 'never edits code' line, and cannot proceed without a decision
findings.suggested_fix: Add a plan sentence: both skills remain ticket-filing (never-edits-code), so the three statements are retained verbatim in each skill's corresponding files; add an AC asserting the tidying janitor SKILL.md still states 'never edits code'.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the success-metric wording with the parent's deliverable-6 ruling: either note that the per-ticket attribution measure REPLACES the operator comment's 'measured on `main` a week later' mechanism (citing the main-delta-is-invisible rationale) or realign to the parent's phrasing, so the leaf does not read as silently redefining the authorized metric.
evidence: Parent operator ruling 2026-11-02, deliverable 6: '...with a per-run ticket budget and a success metric measured on `main` a week later rather than by tickets filed.'
Leaf: 'a run is scored by what LANDED, attributed to the run: the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets and summing the merged diffs of exactly those'

Leaf: 'A bare `main`-to-`main` delta cannot score a tidying run: `main` moved +54,961/-26,221 over 114 commits in the 7 days to `e642101fb56`, so a run's few hundred deleted lines are invisible in it'

Parent's binding Acceptance Criterion for 6b48 only requires the SKILL.md to 'admit only deletions and collapses, and name its budget' — it does NOT pin the main-delta mechanism, so this is a wording/mechanism mismatch against the operator-comment phrasing rather than a contradiction of a binding AC; the leaf preserves the operator's core 'rather than by tickets filed' intent.
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the success-metric MECHANISM relative to the parent's operator ruling: the parent's deliverable 6 says the metric is 'a success metric measured on `main` a week later rather than by tickets filed,' but the leaf explicitly rejects a main-to-main delta and substitutes per-ticket attribution (the next run sums the merged diffs of exactly the previous run's own tickets).
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard (success-metric bullets); vs parent epic 77e3 operator ruling deliverable 6
scenarios: A reviewer comparing the leaf's success metric to the operator's authorized deliverable-6 text notices the main-a-week-later measure was dropped and reads it as scope drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note in the success-metric section stating that the operator's 'measured on main a week later' is superseded by per-ticket attribution for the reason given (main moved +54,961/-26,221, drowning a run's deletions), making the mechanism change an explicit, parent-consistent refinement rather than an unremarked divergence.

findings.checklist_item: State how a ticket is bound to its merged diff (e.g. ticket-id commit trailer / the ticket's recorded file_impact + merge commit) so 'merged-with-delta vs not-merged' and the summed line count are reproducible.
evidence: Plan: 'summing the merged diffs of exactly those, reporting lines removed and mechanisms retired against what each declared, plus the ones never merged'
ABSENCE: no mechanism is named for mapping a ticket to the commit(s) that merged it; rebar does carry ticket ids in completion certificates and file_impact, but the plan does not cite which to use
findings.finding: The scoring step says to sum 'the merged diffs of exactly those' tickets but never names the binding from a ticket to its merged commits (commit trailer, ticket-id-in-commit, or the ticket's file_impact / completion certificate). Without a stated binding the 'merged-with-delta vs not-merged' determination is underspecified.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard: 'summing the merged diffs of exactly those, reporting lines removed and mechanisms retired'; AC 'Its success metric is what merged from the run's own tickets'
scenarios: A ticket's deletion landed across several commits, or alongside unrelated changes, and the next run must isolate that ticket's merged diff
A ticket was merged but its lines later re-added by an intervening feature, making 'lines removed' ambiguous at scoring time

findings.location: Plan 'The change' and AC-12; examples/agent-skills/README.md:17, docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md:7
